title: 92. Quantitative Relationships & Measurement: Writing Ratios from Quantities
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Writing a Ratio from Two Quantities
questions.learningObjective: Write the ratio of boys to girls in simplest form from given counts.
questions.question: A class has \(12\) boys and \(15\) girls. What is the ratio of boys to girls in simplest form?
questions.explanation: The ratio of boys to girls is \(12:15\). Divide both terms by \(3\): \(12 \div 3 = 4\) and \(15 \div 3 = 5\). Thus the simplified ratio is \(4:5\). The alternative uses boys-to-total rather than boys-to-girls.
questions.hint: Write the two quantities in the order requested, then divide both terms by their common factor.

questions.concept: Writing a Ratio from Recipe Quantities
questions.learningObjective: Write the ratio of flour to sugar from given quantities.
questions.question: A recipe uses \(2\) cups of flour and \(3\) cups of sugar. What is the ratio of flour to sugar?
questions.explanation: Flour is named first, so the ratio is \(2\) cups to \(3\) cups, written \(2:3\). The ratio \(3:2\) reverses the order and represents sugar to flour.
questions.hint: The order of the ratio must match the order of the quantities named.

questions.learningObjective: Write the ratio of wins to losses in simplest form.
questions.question: A team won \(8\) games and lost \(4\) games. What is the ratio of wins to losses in simplest form?
questions.explanation: The ratio of wins to losses is \(8:4\). Dividing both terms by \(4\) gives \(2:1\). The alternative uses wins-to-total rather than wins-to-losses.
questions.hint: Keep wins first and losses second, then divide both terms by their greatest common factor.

questions.learningObjective: Write the ratio of red marbles to blue marbles in simplest form.
questions.question: A bag contains \(6\) red marbles and \(9\) blue marbles. What is the ratio of red marbles to blue marbles in simplest form?
questions.explanation: The ratio of red marbles to blue marbles is \(6:9\). Dividing both terms by \(3\) gives \(2:3\). The alternative uses red-to-total rather than red-to-blue.
questions.hint: Keep the named quantities in the requested order and reduce using a common factor.

questions.learningObjective: Write a ratio comparing times after converting to the same unit.
questions.question: What is the ratio of \(30\) minutes to \(2\) hours in simplest form?
questions.explanation: Convert \(2\) hours to minutes: \(2 \times 60 = 120\) minutes. The ratio is \(30:120\). Dividing both terms by \(30\) gives \(1:4\).
questions.hint: Convert both quantities to the same unit before writing the ratio.

questions.learningObjective: Write a ratio comparing lengths after converting to the same unit.
questions.question: What is the ratio of \(45\text{ cm}\) to \(1.5\text{ m}\) in simplest form?
questions.explanation: Convert \(1.5\text{ m}\) to centimetres: \(1.5 \times 100 = 150\text{ cm}\). The ratio is \(45:150\). Dividing both terms by \(15\) gives \(3:10\).
questions.hint: Convert metres to centimetres, then simplify the resulting ratio.

questions.concept: Ratio of a Total to a Part
questions.learningObjective: Write the ratio of total animals to cats from given counts.
questions.question: There are \(5\) cats and \(7\) dogs in a pet shelter. What is the ratio of the total number of animals to the number of cats?
questions.explanation: The total number of animals is \(5+7=12\). The number of cats is \(5\). The ratio of total animals to cats is \(12:5\). The alternative compares dogs with cats rather than the total with cats.
questions.hint: First find the total number of animals, then write the ratio in the requested order.

questions.concept: Ratio of a Part to a Total
questions.learningObjective: Write the ratio of girls to total students in simplest form.
questions.question: A class has \(18\) girls and \(12\) boys. What is the ratio of girls to the total number of students in simplest form?
questions.explanation: The total number of students is \(18+12=30\). The ratio of girls to total students is \(18:30\). Dividing both terms by \(6\) gives \(3:5\). The alternative uses girls-to-boys rather than girls-to-total.
questions.hint: Find the total first, then simplify the ratio of girls to total students.

questions.concept: Writing a Ratio from Mixture Quantities
questions.learningObjective: Write the ratio of water to concentrate in simplest form from given volumes.
questions.question: A mixture contains \(4\text{ L}\) of concentrate and \(14\text{ L}\) of water. What is the ratio of water to concentrate in simplest form?
questions.explanation: The ratio of water to concentrate is \(14:4\). Dividing both terms by \(2\) gives \(7:2\). The ratio \(2:7\) would represent concentrate to water.
questions.hint: Put water first and concentrate second, then simplify the ratio.

questions.concept: Ratio of a Part to a Total from Three Quantities
questions.learningObjective: Write the ratio of sugar to total mixture from three given quantities.
questions.question: A recipe uses \(250\text{ g}\) of flour, \(150\text{ g}\) of sugar, and \(100\text{ g}\) of butter. What is the ratio of sugar to the total mass of the mixture in simplest form?
questions.explanation: The total mass is \(250+150+100=500\text{ g}\). The mass of sugar is \(150\text{ g}\). The ratio of sugar to total mass is \(150:500\). Dividing both terms by \(50\) gives \(3:10\). The alternative compares sugar with the other ingredients rather than with the entire mixture.
questions.hint: Add all three quantities to find the total, then simplify the ratio of sugar to total.
